data.title: Financials drag Indian shares down on profit-taking after four-week rally
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares fell on Monday as broad-based profit-taking set in after a four-week winning streak driven by renewed foreign inflows, easing oil prices and a global selloff in AI-linked stocks.

The Nifty 50 fell 0.65% to 25,636 and the Sensex dropped 0.61% to 83,417.69, as of 10:16 a.m. IST (0446 GMT).

They rose about 0.8% each at the open, before reversing gains.

Fourteen of the 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps and mid-caps lost 0.6% each.

Banks and private banks (.NIFPVTBNK), which had climbed 19.1% and 18.8% over the past four weeks, dropped 1.9% each, dragging the benchmarks.

Financials lost 1.3%, and state-owned lenders fell 2.4% on the day, after gaining 18.3% and 22.4% over the last four weeks.

Metals slid 2.4%, tracking weaker global metal prices and a stronger dollar as concerns over the AI outlook and US rate hikes weighed on sentiment.

Despite the session's losses, the Nifty and Sensex are up 11.4% and 12.2% in November, with both blue-chip gauges spending much of the month in overbought territory.

"While this indicates strengthening bullish momentum, the relative strength index in a higher momentum zone could trigger intermittent profit booking or consolidation in the benchmarks," said Hitesh Tailor, research analyst at Choice Broking.

The recent rally was powered by foreign investors buying a record $13 billion of Indian stocks so far in November, trimming year-to-date outflows to $18.4 billion, below the all-time high outflows of 2025.

Indian markets, due to their limited exposure to AI in the listed space, have emerged as the destination for foreign investors seeking to diversify from the crowded global AI trade. The rally has also been driven by a revival in earnings growth and steady economic growth momentum.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) fell 1% as the AI trade reversal continued.

Among stocks, Tata Steel fell 5.5% and APL Apollo Tubes slid 14.9%.

Tata Steel said it will acquire an initial 26.38% stake in APL Apollo for about $1.67 billion to expand its downstream steel business, a day after agreeing to sell its tubes and colour-coated steel business to APL Apollo.

data.title: SLS Stock Logs Best Week In 6 Years — Why Did The CEO Sell Shares After Its Leukemia Trial Win?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Three Sellas executives sold nearly $717,000 in shares under the same tax requirement.
  • Sellas raised $172.5 million at $13 a share and expects to keep $161.8 million after fees.
  • Median survival hit 24 months with Sellas’ leukemia vaccine, compared with 14.7 months on the best available treatment.

Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) capped their best week in nearly six years after a Phase 3 leukemia trial showed that its experimental vaccine helped patients live longer. Yet the biotech’s latest insider filings show CEO Angelos Stergiou sold more than $510,000 in stock shortly after the trial announcement. The answer lies in taxes tied to performance-based stock awards. This comes amid a $172.5 million capital raise as it prepares for its next regulatory milestones.

SLS stock jumped 156% last week after the results, then fell for three straight sessions. Even then, shares ended Friday at $13.66, up nearly 74% for the week.

Regal Trial Win Triggers Tax Bill For SLS Executives

When the Phase 3 Regal trial met its survival goal, Stergiou and two other executives earned shares that Sellas had awarded them on that condition. The awards came with a tax bill, and the company required all three to sell enough shares to cover it. Last week, Stergiou sold 26,606 shares at $19.178 each. He still directly owned more than 1.73 million shares afterward.

CFO John Burns sold 3,831 shares for about $73,471, leaving him with 558,893. Chief Development Officer Dragan Cicic sold 6,933 shares for about $132,961 and retained 557,361. All three sold at the same price that day, bringing the total to 37,370 shares worth about $716,682.

Sellas’ Stock Offering Grows To $172.5M

Sellas also closed its public offering on Friday. The original $150 million deal grew to $172.5 million when the underwriters bought another 1.73 million shares. In total, Sellas sold 13.27 million new shares at $13 each. This was 28% below Wednesday’s close of $17.95, but still 74% above Monday’s close of $7.47, before the trial results.

Sellas expects to keep $161.8 million after fees, more than the $134.7 million it held in cash and cash equivalents at the end of September. It plans to use the money to fund clinical trials, prepare for a possible drug launch and cover day-to-day costs. “This financing significantly strengthens our balance sheet, giving us the capital runway to execute through our most critical upcoming milestones,” Stergiou said on LinkedIn.

The Survival Data SLS Plans To Take To FDA

Patients who received Sellas’ leukemia vaccine, Galinpepimut-S (GPS), lived a median of 24 months, compared with 14.7 months for those given the best available treatment. The Phase 3 Regal trial enrolled 126 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who were in a second or later remission and could not undergo a stem cell transplant.  The vaccine reduced the risk of death by 41% over the study period, which is a statistically significant result.

“We had guided that we would deliver topline primary endpoint results—and this week, we delivered,” Stergiou said. He added that Sellas is finishing its analysis and working with the trial’s lead investigator, Hagop Kantarjian, to present the full findings at a major medical conference and publish them in a peer-reviewed journal.

Sellas plans to request an FDA meeting as soon as possible to confirm what it needs to include in its application. The company aims to file for approval in the first half of 2027 and will seek expedited review. “Moments like this don’t happen overnight,” Stergious said, adding: “Exciting months ahead!”

How Do Retail Traders Feel About SLS?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS jumped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ ;eve;s a week ago amid ‘extremely high’ message volume.

One user said, “$SLS Imagine being the CEO of $MRK , $JNJ or any other top BP and trying to explain to the Board that your competitor bought Sellas because you were not quick enough to pull the trigger?”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said GPS, SLS009 and Sellas’ broader WT1 immunotherapy platform could justify a $20 billion buyout, or about $92.25 a share. “Acquiring SELLAS today carries development risk, but waiting could mean paying billions more for the same technologies,” the user said.

View this Stocktwits post

SLS stock has surged 262% year-to-date.

data.title: China sets 2030 targets to boost support for older people, childcare
data.description:
China is introducing measures to upgrade care facilities for older people and children by 2030, aiming to adapt to a rapidly aging population and falling birth rates, a government blueprint showed on Monday.

Authorities will advance both infrastructure investment and service quality to "better align the supply of elderly care and childcare services with the needs of the public," according to the plan published on the website of the National Development and Reform Commission and jointly guided by the civil affairs, health and education ministries.

By 2030, nursing care beds will account for 73% of all beds in elderly care institutions, while community care facility coverage for older people will reach 70% and around 2,000 aging public nursing homes will be renovated, the document said.

To boost childcare capacity, authorities aim to extend childcare service centres across all prefecture-level cities and raise the enrolment rate for children under age 3 by 6 percentage points from 2025 levels.

The plan also supports kindergartens in renovating or expanding to offer classes for 2-to-3-year-olds, and encourages employers to use their own premises to provide workplace childcare. Projects will be backed by central budget funds, local government special bonds and commercial credit, alongside tighter supervision of prepaid nursing home fees to curb fraud.

Chinese authorities have rolled out a range of measures in recent years to encourage marriage and childbearing, including family subsidies, childcare support and reducing childbirth-related medical costs, but births have continued to fall.

China's population shrank for a fourth consecutive year in 2025 as its birth rate dropped to a record low, and demographers warn of a similar trend in 2026.

Official data showed China's old-age dependency ratio surpassed its child dependency ratio for the first time in 2025, meaning its workforce now supports more older people than children.

data.title: Asian Regulators Step Efforts to Calm AI-Driven Market Turmoil
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Regulators and market operators in China, South Korea and Taiwan have rolled out emergency measures to arrest the turmoil sparked by the global rout in artificial-intelligence stocks.

Asian markets remained volatile on Monday, though some improvements suggest the moves could be soothing worries about the unwinding of the AI investment boom.

China's tech-heavy ChiNext index reversed morning declines to gain 1.2% in afternoon trading, while Taiwan's Taiex benchmark also rebounded, last up 2.9%.

South Korea's Kospi pared earlier losses of as much as 5.8% to last sit 3.2% lower.

Asian authorities' efforts to quell volatility come in the wake of the Nvidia scandal that led to Jensen Huang's exit.

Huang's departure spurred a wave of selloffs in AI-related names as investors worried about the unravelling of billions in financing that he orchestrated, and which have underpinned the industry's growth.

A turbulent debut by Anthropic then capped a $4 trillion wipeout in the U.S. last week, moves mirrored in Asia, where Taiwan's Taiex suffered its worst week since 1990. South Korea's benchmark Kospi has lost nearly 18% in the month to date.

South Korea and Taiwan had moved to stem the bleeding in AI and tech shares earlier this month, and are now bulking up market defenses.

In Seoul, officials are preparing a market-stabilization fund and vowed to step up scrutiny of trading activity, including illegal short selling and market manipulation during a three-month period. They will also ease limits on daily share buybacks for three months starting Tuesday.

South Korea's Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il on Monday warned that volatility in the semiconductor sector could amplify fluctuations in the broader economy, noting that external risks remain high amid regulatory uncertainty about AI, geopolitical tensions and rising interest rates.

Taiwan has already activated its own market-stabilization fund, deploying support for local stocks since Nov. 6. Established in 2000, the Taiwanese fund has about $15 billion of capital at its disposal and steps in during times of crisis, like the Covid pandemic.

The island's Financial Supervisory Commission said Saturday that it has tightened short-selling rules, and raised the minimum margin requirement for short selling to 150% from 130% to discourage traders from taking speculative short positions.

The stabilization fund said Taiwanese market fundamentals remain strong and selling by foreign investors has gradually subsided.

In China, the three main stock exchanges said over the weekend that they will cut the minimum requirement for margin financing to 80% from 100% effective Nov. 30.

The move is aimed at helping moderately increase leverage, improve market liquidity, and promote stable, healthy market development, the operators said.

According to Chinese state media outlet Xinhua, the adjustment could theoretically free up nearly 400 billion yuan, or roughly $60 billion, in incremental funds.

  • Jihye Lee contributed to the report

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: US futures bounce as Asia scrambles to shore up stocks after AI-driven rout
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq 100 futures rise 3%
  • Taiwan stocks bounce 2%; KOSPI falls as much as 5% before steadying
  • Investors jumpy, nervous as AI trade falters

By Tom Westbrook

US stock futures rose on Monday while authorities readied to prop up sliding stock markets in Asia, after a wipeout last week for the tech and chip stocks at the centre of the AI boom.

Investors are questioning whether the vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI tools will generate profits large and fast enough to repay lenders.

Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its largest weekly decline since pandemic panic gripped markets in March 2020, while the fall in Taiwan's chipmaker-heavy benchmark was the biggest since 1990.

On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures bounced nearly 3% in Asia and S&P 500 futures rose by 2%, while Taiwan stocks TWSE:TAIEX rose 2%. European futures were steady.

But the rout deepened for South Korea's KOSPI index , which fell about 5% to a 10-month low.

The KOSPI was global equities' leading light in the first half of this year, as bets on chip demand more than doubled the index's value in six months.

In the reckoning, the index has halved from its peak and South Korea's finance minister on Monday reiterated plans to stabilise the market, if necessary, which helped to steady shares.

Taiwan's financial regulator has ordered a tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China, stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

"We need to be a bit careful here," said portfolio strategist Damien Boey at Wilson Asset Management in Sydney.

A suite of mood indicators he tracks showed US markets spent three sessions in "panic" territory last week, he said. That can sometimes signal the worst is over, but in this case traders might have a hard time finding a reason for a turnaround.

"If you don't have a policy pivot (at central banks) then there's no catalyst for a risk appetite panic to turn into a durable bounce," he said, leaving investors jumpy and unsure.

Japanese markets were closed for a holiday on Monday but futures indicated selling pressure, while markets in Hong Kong and China sank to new multi-month lows. Bonds and the dollar, safe-haven assets that rose sharply on Friday, mostly held gains.

AI TRADE TURNS

For about four years since the launch of chatbot ChatGPT, the "AI trade" has lifted a wide range of stocks, from chip to switch and cable makers to electricity generators on the assumption of explosive growth in computing demand.

According to analysts, AI spending is staying solid, with Morgan Stanley forecasting a rise next year in hyperscaler capital expenditure of more than 70% to top $1.6 trillion.

But the mood in the market has shifted drastically.

The exit of Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO nicknamed the "godfather of AI", has called the chipmaker's strategy of financing some of its customers into question. The faltering debut of AI leader Anthropic , which on Friday closed 8.5% lower on its first full day of trading, showed traders turning fickle.

Over the year to date, a Hong Kong index of AI stocks spanning Chinese chipmakers and AI companies is down nearly 60%.

The next test, besides the price performance of US markets this week, will be the results and outlook from computer maker Dell on Tuesday and, next month, whether the US Federal Reserve raises interest rates as investors expect.

The dollar's strength lifted it above 159 yen briefly on Monday, kept the euro below $1.10 and pinned the mood-sensitive New Zealand dollar near a 17-year low.

data.title: Beijing steps up market rescue with record 90B yuan ETF purchases
data.description:
China’s state-backed funds invested a record 90B yuan ($13.5B) in ETFs on Friday, stepping up efforts to support the country’s stock market as a prolonged selloff pushed the benchmark CSI 300 Index into bear-market territory.

The purchases across nine ETFs associated with China’s so-called national team exceeded the previous record of 87 billion yuan set during the April 2025 market downturn triggered by US tariffs, according to Bloomberg.

The Harvest CSI 300 ETF attracted a record 23B yuan in inflows, while the ChinaAMC SSE 50 ETF received an all-time high of 21.7B yuan.

The latest buying comes as Chinese equities face mounting pressure from an artificial intelligence-led technology selloff. The CSI 300 has declined in all but two weeks since August, with state-backed purchases yet to reverse the broader market downturn.

Alongside the ETF purchases, China's three main stock exchanges announced measures to support market liquidity. The Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges will lower the minimum margin financing requirement for investors buying securities with borrowed funds to 80% from 100%, effective November 30. The change, approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, reverses a tightening introduced in January.

The outstanding balance of margin trades fell 1.9% on Friday, marking its steepest decline since July 20, according to the report.

The Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges also announced plans to reduce trading fees, while the Shenzhen Stock Exchange proposed introducing a market-making mechanism on its ChiNext startup board to help curb share-price swings and improve market liquidity.

The record ETF purchases and easing of margin financing requirements underscore Beijing’s efforts to support market liquidity and investor confidence amid persistent selling pressure.

data.title: Bitcoin holders realize $17B in losses over 30 days
data.description:
Bitcoin holders realized $17 billion in losses over the past 30 days. That is money actually lost on coins that were sold, not hypothetical drawdowns on a screen.

The figure lands during a rough November for the market. Bitcoin's price slide pushed even patient, long-term investors to hit the sell button at a loss, and the damage now extends from individual wallets to corporate balance sheets and the stocks built around them.

A realized loss happens when a coin moves at a lower price than it last moved at. Think of it as the difference between your house losing value on Zillow and actually selling it for less than you paid. Only the second one counts here.

The gross number tells one part of the story. A cleaner read comes from CryptoQuant's 30-day net realized profit/loss metric, which offsets the gains some sellers booked against the losses others took.

As of November 19, that net figure stood at -$8.4 billion, according to CryptoQuant. That marks its lowest level since the summer.

The turn was sharp. In mid-October, the same metric sat at a positive +$13.1 billion, meaning sellers were mostly cashing out winners. It flipped into negative territory on November 11.

From there, the pace picked up. Net losses grew by $5.4 billion across the four days from November 15 to 18.

November 16 stood out on its own. That single day recorded a loss of $1.69 billion, a single-day record within the current sell-off.

The pressure came as Bitcoin's price fell toward $62,000 and briefly dipped below it.

The long-term holder SOPR fell to 0.73. SOPR, or Spent Output Profit Ratio, compares the price a coin sells at with the price it was acquired at. A reading of 1 means breakeven.

At 0.73, coins moved by long-term holders during the sell-off were sold at an average loss of about 27%.

Strategy, one of the largest corporate holders of Bitcoin, is facing approximately $17 billion in paper losses on its treasury.

The company holds 850,849 BTC, acquired for around $64.2 billion at an average price of $75,452 per coin. With Bitcoin trading near $55,500 to $56,000 in that analysis, the stack is valued at roughly $47.2 billion.

The key word is paper. Strategy has not sold, so these losses are unrealized. The company remains committed to its long-term investment approach and maintains a robust net reserve position.

The ripple effects reach shareholders as well. A separate analysis by 10X Research indicates that retail investors have lost approximately $17 billion on shares of Bitcoin treasury firms as the premiums on those stocks collapsed.

That premium was the extra amount investors paid for treasury company shares above the value of the Bitcoin they held. When it shrinks, shareholders lose money on top of whatever Bitcoin itself does.

CryptoQuant's 30-day net realized loss hit -$30 billion in February and -$18.4 billion in June 2026. Against those benchmarks, the current -$8.4 billion looks almost restrained.

The swing from +$13.1 billion in mid-October to -$8.4 billion by November 19 is what makes this episode notable. The speed of the reversal, more than its size, is what caught holders off guard.

data.title: Foodlink F&B Holdings' ₹361-crore IPO to open on Nov 26; price band set at ₹181-191
data.description:
Foodlink F&B Holdings (India) Ltd, a luxury food services company, is looking to raise ₹361 crore through its maiden public offering, which will open for subscription on November 26, with a price band of ₹181-191 per share.

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) will close on November 30, while bidding for anchor investors will take place on November 25, according to the public announcement on Monday.

The public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to ₹192 crore and an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 88,35,382 equity shares worth ₹168.76 crore by existing shareholders.

At the upper end of the price band, the total issue size works out to ₹360.76 crore.

The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the fresh issue towards setting up one new centralised kitchen and two new banquets, as per the RHP (Red Herring Prospectus).

A portion of the proceeds will also be invested in its material subsidiary, Foodlink Global Restaurants & Catering Services LLC, to fund the setting up of four new casual dining restaurants.

The funds will additionally be used for repayment or prepayment of outstanding borrowings and general corporate purposes.

Foodlink F&B Holdings (India) is a luxury food services business focused on providing curated culinary experiences. Its business model comprises events catering, casual dining restaurants and cloud kitchens, and banquets and integrated food and beverage services.

The company operates several casual dining restaurants and cloud kitchens under brands such as India Bistro, Art of Dum, China Bistro and Glocal in India and the United Arab Emirates.

In its events catering business, the company counts Hardcastle Restaurants, the master franchisee operator of McDonald's in western and southern India, Zee Entertainment and Greenply among its clients.

Foodlink is expected to make its stock market debut on December 3.

Equirus Capital and JM Financial are the book-running lead managers for the issue, while MUFG Intime India is the registrar.

data.title: Tata Steel to Buy Stake in Indian Steel Tubes Maker in Near $1.7B Deal
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat

Tata Steel agreed Monday to buy a 26.6% stake in APL Apollo Tubes for $1.67 billion, paving the way to take control of the smaller Indian steel tubes maker.

Tata Steel will pay 2,100 Indian rupees, equivalent to $22.67, a share for the stake held by APL Apollo's promoters, the steelmaker said in an exchange filing Monday.

Tata Steel will also make an open offer for a further 26% stake at 2,301.40 rupees a share.

On Sunday, Tata Steel agreed to sell its steel tubes business and its coated steel unit, Tata Steel Colors, to APL Apollo for 280 billion rupees.

APL Apollo would fund the acquisition through a mix of acquisition financing and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalization to de-risk the balance sheet, the statement said.

After the deal closes, APL Apollo will become Tata Steel's main vehicle for growth in steel tubes and coated steel, with a combined capacity of 7.5 million tons a year.

Tata Steel shares are trading 5.8% lower and APL Apollo is down 15%.

Write to P.R. Venkat at venkat.pr@wsj.com

data.title: Ashoka Buildcon, Texmaco Rail, RVNL, Premier Explosives shares gain up to 7% on major order wins
data.description:
Shares of Ashoka Buildcon, Texmaco Rail and Engineering, Apollo Micro Systems, Premier Explosives, RVNL and Ratnaveer Precision Engineering gained up to 7% on Monday, November 23, after the companies reported order wins over the weekend.

Ashoka Buildcon

The company on Friday, November 20, after market hours said its joint venture with SAM India has been declared the lowest bidder for the projects of the Rajasthan Metro Rail Corporation Ltd worth ₹2,758.31 crore.

The company said it is the lead member of its JV with SAM India.

Both projects include the design and construction of elevated viaduct and 12 elevated stations (including architectural finishing) on lump sump contract basis, with a defect liability period of 12 months.

While one project is under the Jaipur Metro Phase- 11 MRTS - Package 3, the other one also includes modification of part operational corridor of Phase 1 and construction of Khasa Kothi (Phase 1) station under the Jaipur Metro Phase- 11 MRTS Package 4.

Both projects are to be executed in 36 months.

While the first project is worth ₹1,130.31 crore, the second is worth ₹1,628 crore.

This comes after Ashoka Buildcon had informed the exchanges on Friday that it had received the Letter of Acceptance (LoA) for a project worth ₹1,465 crore from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). Last week, the company had informed the exchanges that it had emerged as the lowest bidder for the 1,465 crore NHAI expressway project.

Shares of Ashoka Buildcon are trading 4.8% higher on Monday at ₹116.3. The stock is down 30% so far this year.

Texmaco Rail and Engineering

The company informed the exchanges on Saturday, November 21, that it has received two letters of intent (LoIs) aggregating to ₹230.58 crore.

One is from JSW Rail Infra Logistics Pvt Ltd for a project worth ₹102.57 crore. It is for the manufacturing and supply of 246 wagos comprising BFNSM1 and BVCM wagons. It is to be executed by February 2027.

The second quarter is from JSW (South) Rail Logistics Pvt Ltd worth ₹128.01 crore. It is for the manufacturing and supply of 307 wagons comprising BFNSM1 and BVCM wagons. It is to be completed by May 2027.

Shares of Texamco Rail and Engineering were up 1.3% at ₹112.82 apiece. The stock has risen 14.5% in the past month but has fallen 17.4% in 2026, so far.

Premier Explosives

Shares of Apollo Micro Systems' unit Premier Explosives gained up to 7% on Monday after the company informed the exchanges on Saturday, November 21, that it has received an export order for approximately ₹311 crore from an international entity.

The order is for the manufacture and supply of defence explosives and is to be delivered within 12 months. Apollo Micro is set to acquire stake in Premier Explosives.

Shares of Premier Explosives are trading 9% higher on Monday at ₹600. The stock is up 15% so far this year. On the other hand, shares of Apollo Micro Systems are trading 0.5% higher at ₹430.

RVNL

The company informed the exchanges on Sunday, November 22, that it has emerged as the lowest bidder for an East Coat Railway project for the augmentation of Vadlapudi Wagon Workshop for the andhancement POH out turn from 300 to 600 wagons at the Wagon Work shop at Vadlapudi, Vishakapatnam. The same is to be completed in 24 months.

The order is worth ₹348.45 crore.

Shares of RVNL are off openings highs of ₹195.95, and are now trading 0.2% lower on Monday at ₹190.65. The stock is still down 50% so far this year.

Ratnavaeer Precision Engineering

The company informed the exchanges on Saturday, November 21, that it has secured a long-term supply agreements and orders for nearly 50% of the planned copper clad laminate (CCL) capacity. The trial runs are excepted in December 2026 to January 2027.

Shares of Ratnaveer Precision Engineering were up 1% at ₹374.1 apiece on Monday. The stock has risen 12.6% in the past month and is up 144.5% this year, so far.

data.title: Aussie Flyers Score a Bold New Airline Choice to Kuala Lumpur as TransNusa Launches Bali-Kul Flights
data.description:
BALI, INDONESIA, Nov 20, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - TransNusa is opening a direct bridge between Bali (DPS) and Kuala Lumpur (KUL), giving passengers from Australia a new, fresh, single-carrier route to Malaysia's capital ahead of the year-end travel season.

This new service creates a smooth one-stop corridor via Denpasar for passengers departing Melbourne and Perth complete with single-ticket convenience, through-checked baggage, a minimum of 20kgs of free checked baggage, excluding 7kgs of hand-carry across all fare tiers. Reservations are now open at transnusa.co.id, with commemorative launch fares starting from as low as USD83.

Underscoring the commercial importance of the route, TransNusa Group Chief Executive Officer, Datuk Bernard Francis noted that linking Melbourne and Perth to Kuala Lumpur via Bali gives passengers from Australia greater itinerary control and value.

"Australia is a key commercial growth market for TransNusa, and this launch gives passengers departing Melbourne and Perth a reliable, seamless airline choice into Kuala Lumpur," said Datuk Bernard.

"Whether passengers from Australia are building in a Bali stopover on their way to Malaysia, connecting onward through Kuala Lumpur's long-haul hub to Europe, the Middle East, and across Asia, or pairing a Malaysian trip with our six domestic destinations from Denpasar Lombok, Wakatobi, Bima, Surabaya, Waingapu, and Manado this route turns multi-destination travel into a single, effortless booking.

"By integrating our Malaysian and Indonesian networks directly with our Australian ports, we are giving travellers the freedom to move across Australia, Bali, Malaysia, and the wider archipelago on one airline-backed by flexible service tiers."

The Bali-Kuala Lumpur service marks TransNusa's third international route launched from its Denpasar hub in 2026, following the rollout of direct flights to Phuket in September and Melbourne in October, alongside expanded domestic sectors to Wakatobi, Waingapu, and Surabaya. With Kuala Lumpur joining Melbourne, Perth, Singapore, Phuket, and Guangzhou as direct international feeders into Denpasar, the airline continues to strengthen its multi-hub regional network.

The new route also complements TransNusa's existing Malaysian operations from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur, Subang, and Penang, and from Lampung to Kuala Lumpur, while advancing its partnership with Tourism Malaysia to boost leisure and cultural travel to destinations such as Penang, Perlis, and Langkawi.

Datuk Bernard concluded that as Indonesia's pioneering Premium Service Carrier, TransNusa remains committed to expanding its signature "Beyond Bali" network to offer its regional passengers greater travel flexibility.

Flight Schedule

Commencing December 10, 2026, TransNusa will operate four weekly scheduled services between Bali and Kuala Lumpur every Monday, Thursday, Friday, and Sunday. Outbound Flight 8B 601 will depart I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS) at 11:00 and arrive at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) at 14:05, while the return service, Flight 8B 602, will depart Kuala Lumpur at 14:40 and arrive in Bali at 18:05.*

About TransNusa

Reborn under new management led by seasoned aviation leader Datuk Bernard Francis, TransNusa (PT TransNusa Aviation Mandiri) has rapidly emerged as one of Southeast Asia's most innovative and dynamic airlines. As the Asia-Pacific region's pioneering Premium Service Carrier, TransNusa bridges the gap between traditional low-cost airlines and full-service carriers through its tailored fare tiers SEAT, SEAT PLUS, and FLEXI PRO which deliver flexible baggage allowances, complimentary meals, and priority privileges across its network, alongside an exclusive Premium Plus option offered specifically on its Melbourne Bali route.

Renowned for a series of industry firsts, TransNusa leads the way in developing unique local and underserved routes serving as the first airline to pioneer direct air links to Bali and sought-after eastern Indonesian islands such as Manado, Wakatobi, and Waingapu, as well as launching Indonesia's first-ever scheduled direct flights connecting Bandar Lampung to Kuala Lumpur. Its rapid regional growth and operational excellence also saw TransNusa become the first airline to receive a prestigious Changi Airline Award within a record 17 months of launching Singapore operations, alongside partnering with Airbus to introduce Indonesia's first fully integrated flight and technical digital aviation ecosystem. Operating out of its main hubs in Jakarta and Bali, TransNusa connects travelers seamlessly across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, China, and Australia. To purchase TransNusa tickets, visit www.transnusa.co.id.

Website: transnusa.co.id.

Passengers can purchase tickets directly from TransNusa via its website.

data.title: Nifty hits nine-month high as IT and Auto lead gains; metal stocks drag
data.description:
Benchmark indices opened on a firm note Monday, with the Sensex trading at 84,108.37, up 188.66 points or 0.22 per cent from its previous close of 83,919.71, after opening at 84,421.97. The Nifty 50 stood at 25,842.30, gaining 41.70 points or 0.16 per cent, against a previous close of 25,800.60 and an opening of 25,929.15, as of 9.21 am on November 23, 2026.

The opening follows a strong week for Indian markets. The Nifty gained 2.61 per cent and the Sensex rose more than 2,300 points last week, with both indices closing at nine-month highs. This comes even as Wall Street suffered its worst weekly loss in 18 months, with the S&P 500 falling 8.6 per cent, the Nasdaq shedding 10 per cent and erasing all 2026 gains, and the Dow dropping 8 per cent.

Among Nifty 50 top gainers on Monday, Shriram Finance led with a last traded price of ₹995, up 2.37 per cent from its previous close of ₹972, on a volume of 16.27 lakh shares worth ₹163.43 crore. Apollo Hospitals traded at ₹9,370, up 1.85 per cent from ₹9,200. TCS rose 1.80 per cent to ₹2,419 from a previous close of ₹2,376.20, with 2.74 lakh shares changing hands worth ₹66.46 crore. Maruti Suzuki climbed 1.75 per cent to ₹14,256 from ₹14,011, on volumes of 1.11 lakh shares worth ₹157.79 crore. Tech Mahindra added 1.59 per cent, trading at ₹1,773.90 against a previous close of ₹1,746.20.

On the losing side, Tata Steel was the biggest drag, down 3.79 per cent to ₹171.26 from a previous close of ₹178, with a heavy volume of 174.69 lakh shares worth ₹298.81 crore. Hindalco fell 1.85 per cent to ₹912.35 from ₹929.50. JSW Steel declined 1.53 per cent to ₹1,316.50 from ₹1,337. UltraTech Cement slipped 0.70 per cent to ₹12,848 from ₹12,939. IndiGo was down 0.67 per cent to ₹5,550 from a previous close of ₹5,587.60.

The sectoral picture reflects a sharp divergence. IT and financial stocks are driving gains while metals and cement remain under pressure. PSU Banks were the top-gaining sector last week, rising 6.72 per cent, while metal stocks were the worst performers, down 2.94 per cent.

Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments Limited, noted that "the vicious cycle of FII selling leading to rupee depreciation, triggering more FII selling, has turned into a virtuous cycle of FII buying leading to rupee appreciation triggering more FII buying." Foreign institutional investors bought equities worth ₹10,308 crore on a net basis on Friday, their ninth consecutive session of buying. Domestic institutions, however, sold equities worth ₹4,859 crore for the third straight session.

The Indian rupee strengthened 1.66 per cent last week to close at ₹92.67 per US dollar, a seven-month high. Oil prices offered some relief, with WTI crude trading in the $82–83 per barrel range on ample global supply.

Monday also marks the November F&O monthly expiry, which could amplify intraday moves. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, cautioned that "the market's ability to withstand deteriorating global risk appetite and defend key support levels will be critical in determining whether the uptrend retains momentum or gives way to profit-booking."

Technically, analysts broadly see 25,500 on the Nifty and 83,000 on the Sensex as key support, with Shrikant Chouhan of Kotak Neo noting that "a sustained move above 26,300/86,000 would take the index into blue-sky territory." Bank Nifty closed at a fresh lifetime high of 64,635.20 on Friday. Hitesh Tailor of Choice Broking flagged that RSI at 78.13 signals "strong but overbought momentum," advising against chasing prices at higher levels.

Indian markets will be closed tomorrow, Tuesday November 24, for Guru Nanak Jayanti. The US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and will close early on Friday.
